name: Traditional Cel Animation. This is a supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection.
visualIdentity: Fixed backgrounds with layered character drawings, consistent linework, flat fills, and shadow shapes. Actions animate through distinct drawings with clean transparent compositing. Digital output simulates the cel look and must not imply photographed physical cels. It is a historical technique, distinct from cel-shaded 3D rendering.
suitableUses: Explicitly listed fits include illustrated mascots, anime, cartoon, storybook, or rigged character scenes, and product or explainer scenes with an expressive character. Inferred fit: character-led scenes on simple backgrounds. Painted environments or multiplane-style depth call for a hybrid approach.
limitations: The source gives no numeric limits. The style needs separate background and character layers, plus suitable drawings or a rig for expression. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics, so stateful simulations should be cached. Planned exposure cadence and held states must be preserved.
palette: This is a reference-dependent example, not a canonical palette: background #F6EDD8, foreground #263746, accent_1 #718E9D, accent_2 #BE795F, with no gradient. Task-provided or approved exact colors override these and keep their assigned roles. Foreground on background measures 10.495:1. Accents reach about 3.5:1 against the foreground and are decorative fills only.
motionAndInteraction: Motion keeps the planned drawing exposure rate, held states, and designed trajectories, without automatic in-betweens, springs, or bounce. Video derives all state from seekable composition time. Optional referenced patterns are gaze tracking (illustrated pupils, not viewer tracking), chaptered transitions, and scroll storytelling. Live pointer or scroll input belongs only to interactive delivery.
audio: The source leaves audio unspecified, so these are topic-specific suggestions. Options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen for the audience and objective. Keep speech intelligible, avoid competing vocals and clipping, and verify sync in the final video. Use only authorized assets.
assetRequirements: Supply layered artwork with alpha transparency, consistent dimensions, numbered frame sequences, and a clear layer manifest. Krita can draw frames and export numbered PNG sequences. Load fonts and assets before rendering. Inspect assets for missing files and crop margins, and state any missing assets explicitly.
combinations: Suggested hybrid: style-039 gouache plates for backgrounds, gouache only, with plate palette subordinate to characters. Another suggestion is style-101 restrained multiplane parallax, with nearer layers moving faster and characters locked to the ground layer. Do not describe it as full 3D. Use hybrids only when materials and motion stay compatible.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition and export, using sized compositions, timed clips, and one paused seekable GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines. Run check and snapshot before the delivery render. Remotion is a conditional fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Pixi.js can render layers, and chroma.js can validate colors. Verify decoded frames, audio sync, and loop seams.
